selected_problem: Fresh main canonicalized trailing separators in ChangesetStore.stage, but federated proposal normalization still preserved them. The same regular-file target could therefore be represented as src/a.mjs and src/a.mjs/ during consensus, scoring and context requests even though downstream changeset staging collapses both to src/a.mjs.
decision_basis: This is a direct consistency gap exposed by the freshly merged changeset trailing-separator invariant, not a new product or architecture choice.

Federated proposal normalization already owns canonical change/context path identity before consensus and winner selection, so the cycle reuses the existing boundary rather than adding a new subsystem.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained unavailable with transient HTTP 502; this cycle uses DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY and does not claim a hosted DWAC success receipt.

pre_fix_reality.effect: Equivalent downstream file targets could fail exact-consensus identity and duplicate context/scoring identity before changeset staging canonicalized them.

change: Federated repo-relative normalization now removes trailing separators after POSIX lexical normalization and fails closed if that produces an empty path. Change targets, manifest identity and needs_more_context therefore share the same regular-file trailing-separator identity as ChangesetStore.stage.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: PASS: standalone Node reproduction of the fresh-main normalizer returned distinct src/a.mjs and src/a.mjs/ identities.
validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed federated-generation module content used for the focused replay.
validation.focused_tests: 2/2 PASS: trailing-separator change/context normalization and exact-consensus identity across two providers.
validation.github_actions: not requested; candidate head workflow runs were empty before PR creation

truth_boundary: This closes trailing-separator lexical identity drift in federated regular-file proposal paths. It does not claim filesystem case/Unicode equivalence, parser-grade repository semantics, arbitrary proposal correctness, arbitrary I/O atomicity, or arbitrary complex repository synthesis.
